findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the stamp derivation and mapping mutation land in a SINGLE git commit (or, if two, that the stamp is committed no later than the mapping and never removed before the mapping drops below two projects) so the 'no un-gated window' property in AC7 actually holds.
evidence: Plan: 'the bridge projects set/remove write path re-derives the stamp SYNCHRONOUSLY in the same operation as the mapping mutation ... so no window exists where a multi-project store is un-stamped and an older binary un-gated'
compat.py write_compat_record and init.py:522 _store_compat_unit each write/commit .store-compat.json independently; the mapping write is a separate file

ABSENCE: the plan does not state whether both files land in ONE git commit, nor the required ordering (stamp committed no later than the mapping) — two sequential commits reopen the very window the property denies
findings.finding: The store-compat AC claims the synchronous stamp guarantees 'no window exists where a multi-project store is un-stamped and an older binary un-gated', but .store-compat.json and projects.json are two distinct committed tickets-branch files and the plan never pins the commit atomicity/ordering that would make the claim true.
scenarios: mapping committed first, then a crash/interrupt before the stamp commit → a multi-project projects.json is live with no gate
an older binary fetches the tickets branch between the two commits and treats other projects' tickets as unbound
findings.suggested_fix: State that the bridge projects write path stages both .store-compat.json and projects.json and commits them in one atomic tickets-branch commit under the store write lock; on removal, downgrade the stamp only after the mapping is committed below the multi-project threshold.

evidence: Plan: 'the bridge projects set/remove write path re-derives the stamp SYNCHRONOUSLY in the same operation as the mapping mutation ... so no window exists where a multi-project store is un-stamped'
compat.py write_compat_record and the mapping write are separate fsutil.atomic_write + git add/commit operations; nothing in the plan binds them into one atomic commit
init._store_compat_unit today writes and commits .store-compat.json as its own commit, separate from any mapping write
ABSENCE: the plan names the property (synchronous) and a test for it, but not the failure-case mechanism (what happens if the mapping write commits and the stamp write fails, or vice versa)
findings.finding: The store-compat stamp is claimed to leave 'no window' where a multi-project store is un-stamped, but projects.json (the mapping) and .store-compat.json (the stamp) are two distinct committed tickets-branch files; the plan states the no-window goal without specifying the atomicity/ordering mechanism (single commit, or stamp committed before/with the mapping) that actually guarantees it against a partial or crashed write.
findings.location: Approach / 'Store-compat capability stamp' child; AC7 'the stamp updating in the SAME operation as the mapping write'
findings.suggested_fix: State that bridge projects set/remove stages projects.json and .store-compat.json into a single atomic tickets-branch commit; if a single commit is not feasible, require the stamp (>1-cap) to be committed before the mapping mutation and removed after, so no committed multi-project mapping can exist without its gating stamp.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend child 1734 (or add a child) to fan the three enrichment passes (get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map) out per configured project and assert both projects' enrichment data is present in the merged snapshot, matching parent AC2.
evidence: Parent AC2: 'reconciler test asserts one JQL pair AND one enrichment pass (parent/comment/issuelink maps) per configured project, both projects' enrichment data present in the merged snapshot'.

Parent decomposition, Multi-project inbound fetch child: '_build_snapshot ... iterates the configured project set for the base JQL fan-out AND its three enrichment passes — get_parent_map / get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map called once per project ... single-project enrichment would silently drop parent/comment/issuelink data for every project but one'.
Child 1734 Approach: 'call the existing jqls_for once per project in the store mapping and union the results into the snapshot' — describes only the base search, never the enrichment maps.
Child 1734 has zero acceptance criteria or test scenarios naming get_parent_map / get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map or 'enrichment'.

fetcher.py:590-718 shows the three enrichment merges derive a single project_key ('_query_project ... else derived from the first snapshot key') and call get_parent_map/get_comment_map/get_issuelinks_map exactly once — for one project only.
No other sibling in the roster owns fetcher.py enrichment: a33c only extracts the pagination cluster; d19d is outbound; 462d/67f9/c927/cef7 touch unrelated files.
findings.finding: Parent AC2 requires the reconciler test to assert 'one enrichment pass (parent/comment/issuelink maps) per configured project, both projects' enrichment data present in the merged snapshot', but child 1734 (the only inbound-fetch child) covers only the base JQL pair fan-out and source-project recording — its Approach explicitly limits itself to calling jqls_for per project and unioning the base-search results, and none of its five acceptance criteria mention the parent/comment/issuelink enrichment passes.
scenarios: A store with projects REB and DIG fetches both; the base issues appear in the snapshot, but parent/comment/issuelink data is retrieved for only one project, so tickets from the other project silently lose parent links, comment dedup, and issuelink sync — the exact failure the parent AC2 calls out.
findings.suggested_fix: Widen child 1734's scope and acceptance criteria to iterate the configured project set for the parent/comment/issuelink enrichment merges in _build_snapshot (not just jqls_for), with a test asserting both projects' enrichment maps land in the shared snapshot keyed by issue.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign the synchronous same-operation stamp (bridge projects set/remove re-deriving .store-compat.json required_capabilities in the same operation as the projects.json write) to a named child with a test asserting the property, per parent AC7.

Child 67f9 Approach: 'Registering the name here is inert on its own — nothing stamps it in this story'; its ACs cover classification and the write-gate only.

Child 462d stamps the capability only via the ensure sweep (a backstop), never synchronously in the mapping write; its ACs describe a 'paired test over a one-project and a two-project mapping', not a same-operation property.

Child c927 owns the bridge projects set/remove write path but its body and ACs only assert projects.json and byte-identical bindings.json/prev_snapshot.json — no .store-compat.json write, no synchronous stamp.
The roster is complete (12 children) and contains no separate synchronous-stamp child.
findings.finding: Parent AC7 explicitly requires the store-compat test to cover 'the stamp updating in the SAME operation as the mapping write', and the parent decomposition assigns this to a 'Store-compat capability stamp' child whose write path 're-derives the stamp SYNCHRONOUSLY in the same operation as the mapping mutation'. No sibling in the roster delivers this synchronous same-operation stamp: 67f9 is only the register/expand half ('nothing stamps it in this story'), 462d stamps only via the asynchronous ensure sweep, and c927 (the bridge projects set/remove write path) never touches .store-compat.json in its body or acceptance criteria.
scenarios: An operator runs 'bridge projects set' to add a second project; if the stamp is only written by a later ensure sweep, there is a window where the store is multi-project but un-stamped and an older binary is un-gated — precisely the window parent AC7's same-operation clause exists to close.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add the 'contract/stamp half' store-compat child the parent decomposition describes, or extend c927 to write the compat stamp synchronously in the same set/remove operation and add the same-operation acceptance criterion.
